content.text: : would you be interested in taking a look at resolving this?
Sure, I can do that.
Does anyone else ever had this kind of problem with Fedora builds?
What IDEs are common around the developers?
I think folks either use:
Intellij
Eclipse
vi/emacs/atom
I am not sure if anyone builds in their IDE, however.
Notes:
The failing module is `Fedora Repository Kernel Implementation (ModeShape)`
It's failing with `org.eclipse.aether.transfer.ArtifactNotFoundException: Could not find artifact org.fcrepo:fcrepo-kernel-api:jar:5.0.0-SNAPSHOT`
Observation:
Everything goes smoothly with:
mvn validate -Denforcer.skip=true
It seems the enforcer plugin triggers the problem
...especially the <bannedDependencies> section
The build fails as soon as
<bannedDependencies/> is added
to the enforcer plugin configuration, even without any exclusions configured.
Upgrading the Enforcer plugin to version 3.0.0-M1 (Released July 2017) doesn't help.
It seems the plugins dependency scanning cannot handle this complex dependency setup. I'm stuck here...
Might be related to
https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MNG-3283
and
https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MENFORCER-304
Plugins that require dependency resolution in early phases cause dependency resolution issue
In a multiple modules project,  some enforcer rule can not get sufficient dependency info with default phase validate, causing issues...
: looks like this is a build system issue. What can we do about it? Can we find another way to ban certain dependencies?
: I agree, it seems to be related to the build system, and this issue in particular:
https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MENFORCER-304
Yes, we can explore a different plugin than 'maven-enforcer-plugin' for detecting banned dependencies.
I also note that the following commands work without issue:
> rm -rf ~/.m2/repository/org/fcrepo/*
> mvn -am -pl fcrepo-kernel-modeshape/ clean
And...
> rm -rf ~/.m2/repository/org/fcrepo/*
> mvn -am -pl fcrepo-kernel-modeshape/ install
Is there a use case for needing to execute either:
> mvn -am -pl fcrepo-kernel-modeshape/ validate
..or
> mvn -am -pl fcrepo-kernel-modeshape/ dependency:resolve
..without having built the full application prior?
I'm quoting myself (see the issue description):

Using `mvn install` every time changes have been made to separate modules not only takes too long, but also introduces the problem of "out-dated snaphots" in the local repository if dependencies have not been installed in the right order previously.
Most importantly:
It further corrupts IDE integration (as I noticed using IntelliJ) and seems to raise a problem for individual module testing.

Fedora sub-modules cannot be build/verified/tested before their module dependencies are not installed in the local Maven repository. This exposes resolving dependencies and individual module testing to dependency errors (e.g. building against invalid Kernel API).

A "clean machine" that has never seen Fedora before should be able to execute `mvn validate` and `mvn dependency:resolve` successful. When purging all Fedora related artifacts from the local Maven repository (or starting on a new machine) this is not possible anymore (see attached build report).

Using `mvn install` every time changes have been made to separate modules not only takes too long, but also introduces the problem of "out-dated snaphots" in the local repository if dependencies have not been installed in the right order previously. It further corrupts IDE integration (as I noticed using IntelliJ) and seems to raise a problem for individual module testing.
UPDATE
Running `mvn -am -pl fcrepo-kernel-modeshape validate` the build fails as soon as <bannedDependencies/> is added to the enforcer plugin configuration, even without any exclusions configured.

comments.body: Ralf Claussnitzer: would you be interested in taking a look at resolving this?

Sure, I can do that.

Does anyone else ever had this kind of problem with Fedora builds?

I think folks either use:

  • Intellij
  • Eclipse
  • vi/emacs/atom

I am not sure if anyone builds in their IDE, however.

Notes:

  • The failing module is `Fedora Repository Kernel Implementation (ModeShape)`
  • It's failing with `org.eclipse.aether.transfer.ArtifactNotFoundException: Could not find artifact org.fcrepo:fcrepo-kernel-api:jar:5.0.0-SNAPSHOT`

Observation:

  • Everything goes smoothly with: mvn validate -Denforcer.skip=true
  • It seems the enforcer plugin triggers the problem
  • ...especially the <bannedDependencies> section

The build fails as soon as <bannedDependencies/> is added to the enforcer plugin configuration, even without any exclusions configured.

Upgrading the Enforcer plugin to version 3.0.0-M1 (Released July 2017) doesn't help.

It seems the plugins dependency scanning cannot handle this complex dependency setup. I'm stuck here...

Might be related to https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MNG-3283 and https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MENFORCER-304:

Plugins that require dependency resolution in early phases cause dependency resolution issue

In a multiple modules project, some enforcer rule can not get sufficient dependency info with default phase validate, causing issues...
Andrew Woods: looks like this is a build system issue. What can we do about it? Can we find another way to ban certain dependencies?

Ralf Claussnitzer: I agree, it seems to be related to the build system, and this issue in particular:
https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MENFORCER-304

Yes, we can explore a different plugin than 'maven-enforcer-plugin' for detecting banned dependencies.

..or
> mvn -am -pl fcrepo-kernel-modeshape/ dependency:resolve

..without having built the full application prior?

Using `mvn install` every time changes have been made to separate modules not only takes too long, but also introduces the problem of "out-dated snaphots" in the local repository if dependencies have not been installed in the right order previously.

Most importantly:

It further corrupts IDE integration (as I noticed using IntelliJ) and seems to raise a problem for individual module testing.
